newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes firm, ANS sold at -$0.80.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes firm, ANS sold at -$0.80.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes advanced Wednesday with higher West Texas Intermediate (WTI) prices, and a cargo of Alaskan crude sold at -$0.80 cents, the first deal done in two weeks.

The cargo, sold by BP, contains over 300,000 barresl of 27-degreee Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude and will go to a small Pacific Northwest refiner, traders said. The deal, confirmed by both sides, sold at a discount to April WTI for April delivery.
Traders expect the shipment to reach the refinery in about 10 days.
ANS crude ranged $19.70/19.90 a barrel, up 45 cents from Tuesday.

West Coast refiners last week upped their refining operations, according to API. Operating capacity stood 83.8 percent, a 4.3 percent-point increase, as Exxon and Mobil brought units back from maintenance shutdowns, traders and companies said..
Line 63 stood unchanged at postings plus $0.95 - $1.05.
California heavy grades fell after Texaco lowered their posted prices 50 cents late Tuesday.
